name: Joomla
description: Joomla is an open-source content management system for websites and digital publishing. It supports articles, media, categories, tags, users, permissions, templates, extensions, workflows, and core Web Services APIs.
agentUseSummary: Relay reads only the ID, publication state, and created and modified timestamps for one preselected Joomla article through a fixed core Web Services GET. Joomla's item endpoint returns a larger article representation upstream, so Relay explicitly discards content, identities, categories, tags, media, metadata, custom fields, relationships, and every non-lifecycle field before returning data.

capabilities.label: Read selected article lifecycle
capabilities.description: Read one selected article's ID, publication state, and lifecycle timestamps.

allowed.label: Read selected article lifecycle
allowed.description: Use one fixed core Web Services individual-article GET and return only its lifecycle projection.

blocked.label: Expose content or private site data
blocked.description: Titles, article text, aliases, notes, authors, categories, tags, images, metadata, custom fields, access rules, URLs, identities, and private site data are excluded from Relay output.

blocked.label: Mutate Joomla
blocked.description: Articles, categories, media, users, configuration, extensions, templates, permissions, and every POST, PATCH, DELETE, upload, or other mutation are blocked.

blocked.label: Use broad Joomla access
blocked.description: Article collections, other article IDs, categories, fields, content history, users, menus, modules, templates, extensions, arbitrary routes or queries, redirects, and administration are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Selected Article Lifecycle Read
approvalProfiles.description: Read one selected article's lifecycle projection; content, identities, other resources, administration, and mutations remain blocked.

runtimeSupport.description: Mount one no-input selected-article lifecycle reader backed by Railway's bounded Joomla adapter.
Mount one no-input selected-article lifecycle reader backed by Railway's bounded Joomla adapter.

providerSetup.blocker: An authorized staging site must provide its exact public HTTPS Joomla URL, a dedicated non-Super-User API account with Web Services Login and only the minimum selected-article view access, one article ID, and Fairfax validation.
providerSetup.nextAction: In the provider-console lane, configure the least-privilege staging account and API token, enter the site URL and selected article ID through Relay, then validate exact-resource binding, content-field redaction, redirect and private-DNS denial, insufficient-access denial, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial in Fairfax.

evidence.supports: Official Joomla documentation defines the HTTPS /api/index.php/v1 base, X-Joomla-Token authentication, Web Services Login permission, and GET /content/articles/{id} for one specific article.
Official core source registers CRUD routes at v1/content/articles, allowing Relay to fix execution to only the individual-resource GET route.

Official core source enumerates the article item representation, including content and identity-bearing fields as well as state, created, and modified; this supports Relay's explicit post-response lifecycle projection and redaction requirement.
